newsitem.title: USA: U.S. LPG market steady in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. LPG market steady in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices, after firming in morning activity, were steady to stronger late Friday in quiet trade ahead of the three day holiday weekend, players said.
Prices firmed this morning amid short covering to keep ahead of demand on Monday, when markets will be closed for U.S. President's Day.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, bids for spot propane were about a quarter cent higher from midday to 38.00 cents, with offers remaining at 38.25 cents a gallon.
Prices in the Midwest were notional amid little talk.
Some of Friday's strength was also due to stronger NYMEX March crude oil futures, which ended up 39 cents at $22.41 a barrel.
Meanwhile, a source for Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said Friday the Mexican state-owned oil and gas monopoly is negotiating with Saudi Arabia to extend by two months a contract to import propane.
The source said the additional cargoes will cover Mexico's demand for the LPG until its downed Cactus plant returns online in April.
Some U.S. industry players, however, said late Friday that they doubt the plant will return to full capacity by April, and said Pemex may be in the market for more than two months worth of supply.
